meta.name: Medical SDEC demand and capacity model
meta.organisation: East and North Hertfordshire NHS Trust
meta.notes: Schema v2 rearchitects the model around PER-AREA demand and capacity. SDEC is no longer one floor-wide pool: each physical area carries its own spaces, its own staff roster and its own hourly attendance curve, and the floor-wide figures are the roll-up of those areas. The physical layout is confirmed by the SDEC Service Coordinator; the per-area SPLIT of staffing and demand is a placeholder derived mechanically from the v1 floor-wide seed (SDEC activity export, Apr-Jul 2026, Lister) - see meta.placeholderSplit and the Data to Confirm section in the README.

placeholderSplit.notes: How the v1 floor-wide seed was split across areas, pending real per-area data. STAFFING: the two v1 bay nursing lines (1 WTE B6 NIC + 3 WTE B5, weekday; 2 WTE weekend) were split evenly by whole person across Bay 1 and Bay 2 (2 WTE each weekday, 1 WTE each weekend), preserving the v1 floor total; the EMT (darting/float) lines went to the Darting Rooms; NIC co-ordinator, hello, in-reach and triage nursing roles stayed FLOATING (areaId null) because they work across the whole floor rather than holding patients in one area; every medical line stayed FLOATING on the working assumption that clinicians circulate. DEMAND: the v1 floor-wide patients-present profile was split by referral-source share - hot clinics (5.0/37.2 = 13.4% of attendances) to the Hot Clinic Rooms and the remaining sources (ED pull, GP, follow-up, 111 = 86.6%) to the ambulatory chairs - applying the same hourly shape to both, because no per-area shape exists yet. Bay 1, Bay 2, Darting and Triage therefore carry NO placeholder demand: the referral-source split gives no basis for allocating any to them. Every one of these numbers is editable and none should be treated as observed.

areas.name: Bay 1
areas.notes: 3 trolleys + 3 chairs (confirmed layout). A nursing/concurrency area: patients here are held by bay nurses, so the patients-per-nurse holding capacity applies and is then capped at the 6 physical spaces.

areas.name: Bay 2
areas.notes: 3 trolleys + 3 chairs (confirmed layout). Nursing/concurrency area, same as Bay 1.

areas.name: Ambulatory Chairs
areas.notes: 40 general chairs - the ambulatory zone outside Bay 1/2 (confirmed layout). Not modelled as a nursing/concurrency area because it has no dedicated nursing establishment in the v1 roster; whether these chairs have dedicated staff or float coverage is an open question for the SDEC team. Until then only the 40-space physical ceiling constrains it.

areas.name: Hot Clinic Rooms
areas.notes: 2 hot clinic rooms (confirmed layout). Seeded with the hot-clinic referral-source volume against the floor-wide hourly shape - almost certainly wrong in shape, since hot clinics run to a booked template by day of week and each attendance is a shorter, separate throughput event rather than a bay-length stay.

areas.name: Darting Rooms
areas.notes: 2 darting rooms (confirmed layout), staffed by the EMT lines. Not modelled as a nursing/concurrency area: the v1 EMT lines carried no nursing concurrency capacity (bay = false) and that treatment is preserved. Carries no placeholder demand - darting activity is not separable from the v1 floor-wide profile.

areas.name: Triage Room
areas.notes: There are 2 triage rooms but only 1 is usable for SDEC (the other belongs to AMU), so physicalSpaces = 1. Carries no placeholder demand, and it is an open question whether triage holds patients at all (an occupancy) or is a pure process step with no 'present' time to model.

operatingWindow.notes: SDEC operating window (07:00-24:00 in the seed), applied to every area. Demand and capacity are zeroed outside this window.

assumptions.notes: SDEC-specific planning scalars. defaultNurseRatio is the fallback patients-per-nurse used for a nursing line that holds patients but has no explicit patientsPerHour. floatingAllocation describes how staff with no areaId (the floating pool) are attributed to areas for the per-area view: each hour, the floating pool is shared out in proportion to that area's demand in that hour (medical seeing capacity by medical demand, nursing holding capacity by patients present). This is a display/attribution convention for circulating staff, not a model of which patient goes where; the floor-wide totals are unaffected by it.

areas.notes: NO placeholder demand. The v1 floor-wide profile can only be split by referral source, and no source maps to a bay, so nothing was invented here. Bay 1 therefore shows staffed holding capacity against zero demand until the SDEC team supplies real per-area attendance.
NO placeholder demand - see the Bay 1 note.

PLACEHOLDER: 86.6% of the v1 floor-wide patients-present profile (every referral source except hot clinics), hour by hour. This is where all non-hot-clinic demand sits by default until real per-area attendance data arrives; it is not an observation that these patients occupy a chair rather than a bay.

PLACEHOLDER: 13.4% of the v1 floor-wide patients-present profile - the hot-clinic referral-source share, spread on the floor-wide hourly shape. Real hot clinics run to a booked template (frailty, cardiology, rheumatology, ACT/respiratory) that varies by day of week, so both the shape and the implied length of stay need replacing.
NO placeholder demand. Darting is a short procedural event that the v1 floor-wide profile does not separate out; whether it should be modelled as occupancy at all is an open question.
NO placeholder demand - triage may be a pure process step with no modelled occupancy. Confirm with the SDEC team.

losProfiles.notes: One blended mean length of stay (box-car) applied to EVERY area - areaId null means floor-wide. ~5.0h is data-implied (~213 patient-hours/day weekday / ~42.8 attendances). Per-area length of stay is a known gap: a hot clinic or darting attendance is almost certainly far shorter than a bay stay.

demand.notes: The editable primitive is now area x hour patients-present. demand.areas[].sources keeps the referral-source volumes as a secondary lens per area; they carry no hourly shape of their own and are used to weight the future-state per-source multipliers for that area. Floor-wide demand and floor-wide referral-source volumes are the sum across areas.

lines.name: Consultant
lines.notes: areaId null = floating: circulates across the whole floor. Re-tag to a specific area if a clinician only ever works there.

lines.name: Long Day GP
lines.notes: Floating by default. If this GP only ever runs the hot clinics, re-tag the line to the hot-clinic area.

lines.name: SHO (assumed rate)
lines.notes: SHO patients-per-hour rate is an assumption within the 0.5-1/hr envelope; confirm from job plans.

lines.name: B7 NIC (co-ordinator)
lines.notes: Floating floor-wide co-ordinator; does not hold patients, so it adds no holding capacity to any area.

lines.name: B6 Hello Nurse
lines.notes: Genuinely floor-wide - meets patients wherever they arrive - so deliberately left untagged rather than forced into an area.

lines.name: B6 In-reach Nurse
lines.notes: Works into ED rather than in one SDEC area; left floating.

lines.name: Triage Nurse
lines.notes: Left FLOATING rather than tagged to the Triage Room: triage is a floor-wide function that streams patients into every area. Tag it to the triage area if the room is genuinely staffed as a fixed post.

lines.name: Bay 1 - B6 NIC
lines.notes: PLACEHOLDER SPLIT of the v1 'Bay - B6 NIC' line (1 WTE). Holds patients, so contributes patientsPerHour patients of holding capacity per WTE to Bay 1, capped at Bay 1's physical spaces.

lines.name: Bay 1 - B5 nurse
lines.notes: PLACEHOLDER SPLIT of the v1 'Bay - B5 nurses' line (3 WTE): 1 WTE to Bay 1, 2 WTE to Bay 2, giving each bay an even 2 WTE alongside the B6 NIC. Confirm the real bay-by-bay establishment.

lines.name: Bay 2 - B5 nurses
lines.notes: PLACEHOLDER SPLIT - see the Bay 1 B5 line.

lines.name: Bay 1 - nurse (weekend)
lines.notes: PLACEHOLDER SPLIT of the v1 'Bay nurses (weekend)' line (2 WTE), one per bay.

lines.name: Bay 2 - nurse (weekend)
lines.notes: PLACEHOLDER SPLIT - see the Bay 1 weekend line.

lines.name: EMT (darting)
lines.notes: The v1 'EMT (darting/float)' line, tagged to the Darting Rooms. countsTowardsProfessionCapacity stays false, preserving the v1 treatment that EMTs add no nursing holding capacity.

lines.name: EMT (weekend, darting)
lines.notes: Weekend EMT, tagged to Darting on the same basis as the weekday line.

productivity.notes: PLACEHOLDER for schema consistency with the ED model. The model works off raw WTE x rate with no leave/sickness/headroom adjustment, so this section is NOT wired into the engine.
PLACEHOLDER - see the medical productivity note. Not wired into the engine.

capacity.notes: capacity.lines are floor-wide rows, each tagged with an areaId (null = floating/unassigned). A line's patientsPerHour is the patients-seen-per-hour rate for medical grades and the patients-per-nurse holding figure for nursing lines that hold patients.

standards.notes: The source SDEC tool encodes no staffing rules or benchmarks. This section is intentionally empty (rather than seeded with invented NHS ratios) and is not wired into the engine; it is kept for schema parity with the ED model.

schemes.name: Extend Consultant to 20:00
schemes.note: Senior decision-maker on the floor into the evening peak

schemes.name: Add Twilight Doctor 14:00-24:00
schemes.note: Covers the late arrivals tail so the queue clears before close

schemes.name: Add a Bay Nurse (Day)
schemes.note: One more registered nurse holding patients, 08:00-20:30 - targeted at Bay 1

schemes.name: Weekend Medical Uplift
schemes.note: Second weekend clinician to match weekday cover shape

schemes.name: Open a Third Hot Clinic Room
schemes.note: One more hot clinic room - physical space only, not costed here

future.notes: Future-state levers. A 'capacityAddition' scheme adds staffing lines, tagged to the scheme's areaId (null = floating). A 'physicalSpaceAddition' scheme adds addSpaces physical spaces to its area and carries no staffing cost - capital/estates cost is out of scope. areaSpaceDeltas is the ad-hoc equivalent: spaces added to (or removed from) an area in the future state. The scalar dials (demandMultiplier, losMultiplier, c4cPercent, sourceMultipliers) rescale demand; a per-source multiplier reaches an area in proportion to that area's own referral-source mix, so scaling hot clinics up scales the Hot Clinic Rooms and nothing else. NOTE the deliberate asymmetry carried over from the source tool: c4cPercent (Care Closer to Home diversion) reduces patients-present but NOT arrivals. An add line whose endHour equals 0 means midnight-as-overnight-wrap (e.g. Twilight doctor 14:00-00:00). customCapacityLines carry the net change (wte - baseWte) of any pulled-in and edited baseline lines; empty in the seed.
